passages.title: My part in The Lighthouse
passages.text:
Last term I took part in my school's production of a musical called The Lighthouse. Our drama teacher, Mr Okafor, (1) ____ has written several plays himself, gave me the role of the old lighthouse keeper.

I was delighted, but I soon realised I had more than two hundred lines to learn (2) ____ heart. "You (3) ____ better start learning them today, or you won't be ready," Mr Okafor warned. So every evening my mum read the other characters' lines while I practised mine.

Rehearsals were hard work, but the cast became really close. We helped (4) ____ other with difficult scenes, and the older students gave us useful advice about staying calm on stage.

On the first night I was the (5) ____ nervous I have ever been: my hands were shaking and my mouth was completely dry. But as soon (6) ____ the curtain went up and I heard the audience laugh at my first joke, my nerves disappeared.

We performed the show three times, and every night the hall was full. I'm already hoping to get a part in next year's play.

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (1).
questions.explanation: This is a non-defining relative clause between commas about a person: "Mr Okafor, who has written several plays himself, gave me the role". 'That' cannot be used after a comma in this kind of clause, and 'which' is for things.

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (2).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'learn something by heart', meaning learn it so you can say it from memory: "two hundred lines to learn by heart".

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (3).
questions.explanation: 'Had better' + infinitive without 'to' gives strong advice or a warning: "You had better start learning them today, or you won't be ready," Mr Okafor warned. Only 'had' can go before 'better' here; 'would', 'should' or 'must' + 'better' are not possible.

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (4).
questions.explanation: 'Each other' shows that people do the same thing to one another: the cast "helped each other with difficult scenes".

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (5).
questions.explanation: A superlative with a long adjective is 'the most + adjective', often with 'I have ever been': "I was the most nervous I have ever been". 'Least' is impossible because "my hands were shaking and my mouth was completely dry".

questions.question: Write ONE word for gap (6).
questions.explanation: The time conjunction is as soon as, meaning immediately when: "as soon as the curtain went up … my nerves disappeared". The second as completes the fixed phrase; no other word fits after as soon.
